Afterwards, loading the portal cart onto the employee track, Katia wishes she could have used it. Carl says it would have been a waste, since they could not have hurt him, and that the gift was probably more a message to the brother than a plan to kill him. He promises her a use for it.

beats.headline: Into a goddess's eye
beats.text: Ysalte stands in the corpse of Sister Ines, summoned for a boss event and invulnerable on this floor. Donut's all-caps report tells the rest. Katia gave a crawler an arrow thing, and he stuck it into the goddess's eye. Then he blew himself up, the explosion concentrated on her neck, and her head fell off. The system message names him as her slayer, marked for death by every deity except her sworn enemies. He was her own totem.

beats.headline: Reusable, if unbroken
beats.text: Carl thinks Katia should have had the credit for the goddess, since it took her bolt to do it. Katia is glad she did not: every god is angry at the one who did. Then she pulls it out of her inventory. Funny thing about magical bolts, she says: as long as they don't break, you can reuse them. Carl grins back. The princess meant it for her brother inside Grull, and that possibility is still on the table.

beats.headline: Emberus, fifteen seconds
beats.text: Donut swaps into the room through one of Lucia's loop-de-loop traps with the Scorpion's Bite mount on her back, cocked and loaded with Katia's bolt. She fires true, straight into Emberus's smouldering eye socket. A second shot, one of her Danforth bolts, takes the other eye and holds him in place. The yellow glow winks off: fifteen seconds, and he cannot move. Taranis, seeing his little brother rise, raises a hand and twists his wrist, and with one second left Emberus explodes.

tagline.text: A spiked ball that summons its thrower's god for sixty seconds. Maggie My's, from the Skull Empire, meant to bring the god of pain down on Carl. Carl has it now.
Maggie's grenade, thrown by Carl instead. Emberus arrived, Quan Ch did not get his shot off, and Carl had sixty seconds in which nothing could hurt him.

description.text: These little balls of fun were developed by the nuns of Enyo during the first enlightenment, back when the gods had to compete for worshippers. The nuns would descend upon a village and proselytize to the people about why their goddess was the best. If the villagers didn't immediately fall to their knees in veneration, the nuns would be forced to invoke a more aggressive campaign. A nun would drop a celestial grenade, which would summon Enyo directly into town for a period of sixty seconds. That was usually enough to change the minds of the survivors. Celestial grenades grant the following effects: If the wielder of the grenade has pledged themselves to a specific deity, this grenade will summon their god for sixty seconds. In addition, the wielder will receive a 60-second Divine Intervention aura. If the wielder does not worship a deity, this grenade will summon a random god. They will not receive the Divine Intervention buff.

beats.headline: The ball in the impostor's hand
beats.text: The friend standing in front of Carl is Maggie My wearing him, and she has a round, spiked ball in her hand when Katia's petrify bolt takes her in the head. The ball rolls. Carl dives for it and puts it in his inventory before it can do anything, without knowing what it is. It does not list itself as an explosive. It is a celestial grenade: summon your god for sixty seconds, and stand inside Divine Intervention while it is here.

beats.headline: Bought by the Skull Empire
beats.text: Mordecai's eyes go huge when Carl tosses it to him. These are very expensive and rare, he says, seen on the ninth floor a lot, near the end; using one on a single crawler is like trying to kill a bug with a kinetic strike. The crawler Maggie has been riding gets a message out before he is cut off. She worships Algos, the god of pain, chosen from a scroll sent by her sponsors, Prince Maestro and Crown Prince Stalwart. She got the grenade on this floor.

beats.headline: Thrown from the upper wing
beats.text: The biplane is spiralling down, Orthrus is unconscious, and Quan Ch is closing in, both hands glowing. Carl takes Emberus as his god in mid-air, against every warning in the cookbook, climbs onto the upper wing with Donut clinging to his back, and throws the grenade at Quan. Quan freezes it fifteen feet in front of him with a red bolt. It makes no difference. The ball winks out, and Emberus arrives as a city-sized floating head. Quan never gets his spell off.

beats.headline: Sixty seconds of Divine Intervention
beats.text: The second clause is the one that saves Carl. Imbued with Divine Intervention, he is invulnerable for sixty seconds, and nothing over his head says so. He lands in a valley of the land quadrant unhurt while Donut, on his back, is knocked down to five percent. Emberus leaves early, gone with Orthrus before the minute is out. Quan Ch, who cannot see the buff, hits Carl with lightning while the buff still has a few seconds to run. Carl gets up and punches him in the face.
